bukhari.arabic_anchor: حدثنا آدم، حدثنا شيبان، حدثنا قتادة، عن أنس
bukhari.narrative_anchor: لما عرج بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى السماء قال أتيت على نهر حافتاه قباب اللؤلؤ المجوف فقلت ما هذا يا جبريل قال هذا الكوثر

muslim_candidate.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna -> Ibn Abi Adi -> Sa'id -> Qatada -> Anas -> Malik ibn Sa'sa'a
muslim_candidate.scope: Long Isra report describing four rivers at the lote-tree; the checked display does not identify the river as al-Kawthar and does not carry the Shayban lower chain or the hollow-pearl-bank wording.

comparison.result: Bukhari 4964 directly verifies the chain and report quoted by Ibn Kathir. The checked Muslim 164a report belongs to the broader Isra narrative family but is not the exact R04 witness. No exact Sahih Muslim locator for Ibn Kathir's printed attribution was established in this bounded review.
comparison.preservation_rule: Preserve Ibn Kathir's printed Bukhari-and-Muslim attribution, but do not map Muslim 164a as the exact supporting witness.

arabic_english_fidelity.bukhari: The English rendering preserves the ascent, river, hollow pearl banks, Gabriel question-and-answer, and explicit identification as al-Kawthar.
arabic_english_fidelity.muslim_candidate: The checked English rendering supports an Isra river context only; it does not support the exact al-Kawthar identification sentence used in R04.

disagreements_and_absences: The Ibn Kathir witness explicitly attributes the report to both al-Bukhari and Muslim.
The edition witness directly footnotes the Bukhari occurrence but supplies no exact Muslim number.
The checked Muslim 164a candidate differs in lower chain, narrative scope, and explicit river identification.
This review does not conclude that Ibn Kathir's Muslim attribution is wrong; it records that the exact Muslim occurrence remains source-unlocated.
